---
title: "Comping rhythm: Driving eighths"
subtitle: "For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Driving eighths**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

The chord on every eighth note, the beats a little louder than the off-beats.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Driving eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-quarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Driving eighths, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The chord on every eighth note, beats a little louder. On piano, the right hand bounces from the wrist; on guitar, all downstrokes. Keep it tight with the hi-hat.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Driving eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"eighths"}},{"label":"Quarter-note chords (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Driving eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Driving eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Driving eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"eighths"}}]'></div>
